findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:135 — In Delete, the success-path metric call passes `name` as the kind label instead of `options.Kind`, writing the object name into the `kind` label, producing incorrect metrics and unbounded Prometheus label cardinality

[Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:49 — In Create, when the storage (unified) write fails, the code records `recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` instead of `recordStorageDuration`, attributing the failure to the legacy storage metric

[Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:181 — In Update, the storage-failure path calls `recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` instead of `recordStorageDuration`, mis-attributing unified storage errors to legacy storage

[Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:219 — In DeleteCollection, the async legacy goroutine calls `recordStorageDuration(...)` instead of `recordLegacyDuration(...)`, so legacy delete-collection latency is recorded under the storage metric and the legacy metric is never populated

[High/concurrency] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection goroutines) — Fire-and-forget goroutines derive their context from the request context, so cancellation after the sync storage operation returns will typically cancel the async legacy write before completion, defeating the purpose of the background write; should use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` as the parent

[High/data] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:172-180 — In Update, the legacy goroutine passes the raw `objInfo` to `d.Legacy.Update` instead of the computed/updated object, so legacy storage re-resolves `objInfo.UpdatedObject` against its own possibly different old object, risking version conflicts and divergent data between unified and legacy stores

[Medium/concurrency] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go (all async goroutines) — Background goroutines have no `recover()`; a panic inside LegacyStorage.Create/Update/Delete will now crash the entire apiserver process

[Low/doc_defect] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:130 — In Delete, `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` discards the `log` variable, so the context logger passed to storage lacks the request-scoped fields (name, kind, method) set on `log`

[Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go (legacy goroutines) — Legacy write failures are only counted in metrics and never logged, unlike the previous code that logged them, making dual-write drift undiagnosable except via metrics

[Medium/test_gap] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go — No test verifies that the legacy storage is actually invoked (async goroutine calls are never asserted) and there are no cases exercising legacy-side failure for Create/Update/Delete, so the fire-and-forget behavior is untested

[Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go (TestMode3_Create, "error when creating object in the unified store fails" case) — The test sets up a legacy mock expectation but never sets up the storage mock, so `Storage.Create` hits an unexpected call on the testify mock (panic) rather than returning the intended error; the unified-storage failure path is not actually exercised

[Low/test_gap] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go — Async legacy calls make test results timing-dependent: tests return before the goroutine runs, so any future assertion on legacy mock counts would be flaky; tests should synchronize with the goroutine or inject the timeout/clock

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:49 — In Create, when the storage (unified) write fails, the code records `recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` instead of `recordStorageDuration`, attributing the failure to the legacy storage metric

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, the unified storage write is timed with `startStorage := time.Now()` and executed via `d.Storage.Create(...)`. On error, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` before returning. That records the *storage* failure under the *legacy* duration metric, which is incorrect attribution and verifiably shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:181 — In Update, the storage-failure path calls `recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` instead of `recordStorageDuration`, mis-attributing unified storage errors to legacy storage

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the error path after `d.Storage.Update(...)` does `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` even though the failure occurred in unified `Storage` (and `startStorage` was captured for the storage call). This misattributes storage errors/durations to legacy metrics; it should call `recordStorageDuration(...)` there.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:219 — In DeleteCollection, the async legacy goroutine calls `recordStorageDuration(...)` instead of `recordLegacyDuration(...)`, so legacy delete-collection latency is recorded under the storage metric and the legacy metric is never populated

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, DeleteCollection’s async legacy delete goroutine ends with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)`, even though it is measuring the legacy operation (`d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)`). This misattributes legacy latency/errors to the storage metric and does not populate the legacy metric for this path; it should call `recordLegacyDuration(...)` instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/concurrency] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection goroutines) — Fire-and-forget goroutines derive their context from the request context, so cancellation after the sync storage operation returns will typically cancel the async legacy write before completion, defeating the purpose of the background write; should use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` as the parent

adjudication.rationale: In mode3 Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection, the legacy write is launched in a fire-and-forget goroutine but uses a context derived from the request context (e.g., `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...); ... d.Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection(ctx, ...) }()`). Because `ctx` is the same request-scoped context (only wrapped with a timeout), it will be canceled when the request finishes, so the async legacy operation will often be canceled before completing. This can prevent the intended background legacy write from happening, changing dual-write correctness semantics. Using `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` (or a separate background context) would avoid that cancellation issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/data] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:172-180 — In Update, the legacy goroutine passes the raw `objInfo` to `d.Legacy.Update` instead of the computed/updated object, so legacy storage re-resolves `objInfo.UpdatedObject` against its own possibly different old object, risking version conflicts and divergent data between unified and legacy stores

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the code now calls `d.Storage.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` and then launches a goroutine that calls `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` with the original `objInfo` (see the new goroutine block). The previous implementation computed the updated object once (via `objInfo.UpdatedObject(...)`) based on the unified-store old object and wrapped `objInfo` so legacy would write the same computed object. With the new code, legacy will re-run `UpdatedObject` against its own current/old state, which can differ from unified storage, leading to divergent writes/version conflicts—exactly as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go (all async goroutines) — Background goroutines have no `recover()`; a panic inside LegacyStorage.Create/Update/Delete will now crash the entire apiserver process

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Mode3 now spawns background goroutines for legacy writes in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection (e.g., `go func() { ... d.Legacy.Create(...) ... }()`). These goroutines do not use `defer func(){ if r:=recover(); ... }()` or any other panic containment. In Go, an unrecovered panic in any goroutine will terminate the entire process; additionally, moving the legacy call off the request goroutine means any request-level panic recovery (not shown here) would no longer apply. Thus a panic inside LegacyStorage.* can crash the apiserver, and this risk is introduced/exposed by this diff’s new async goroutines.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go (legacy goroutines) — Legacy write failures are only counted in metrics and never logged, unlike the previous code that logged them, making dual-write drift undiagnosable except via metrics

adjudication.rationale: Verified: in `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy writes are now done in `go func()` blocks for Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection, and the legacy call errors are only passed to `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)` (and in one place even mistakenly to `recordStorageDuration`), with no `log.Error(...)`/`log.WithValues(...).Error(...)` on failure. The previous synchronous code explicitly logged legacy errors (e.g., in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection). This is an observability/diagnosability regression rather than a directly provable functional correctness bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go — No test verifies that the legacy storage is actually invoked (async goroutine calls are never asserted) and there are no cases exercising legacy-side failure for Create/Update/Delete, so the fire-and-forget behavior is untested

adjudication.rationale: In `dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy writes are now done asynchronously in goroutines with a timeout (`go func() { ... d.Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection(...) }()`), i.e., “fire-and-forget”. The new tests in `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go` primarily assert the returned object/error from the unified `Storage` call and do not assert that legacy methods were actually invoked. Although some cases set up legacy expectations via `m.On("Update"/"Create"...)`, the tests never call `m.AssertExpectations(t)` (or otherwise synchronize/wait for the goroutine), so the async legacy calls may never be observed/verified. Additionally, there are no test cases where the legacy call returns an error for Create/Update/Delete to validate that legacy-side failures are handled/recorded without affecting the main operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go (TestMode3_Create, "error when creating object in the unified store fails" case) — The test sets up a legacy mock expectation but never sets up the storage mock, so `Storage.Create` hits an unexpected call on the testify mock (panic) rather than returning the intended error; the unified-storage failure path is not actually exercised

adjudication.rationale: In `TestMode3_Create`, the “unified store fails” case does not set `setupStorageFn`, but it *does* set `m.On("Create", ...)` on the shared `*mock.Mock` used by both `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock`. Since `DualWriterMode3.Create` calls `d.Storage.Create(...)` first, that storage call will match the existing `"Create"` expectation (`failingObj` as the second argument) and return the intended error rather than panicking due to an unexpected call. The finding’s claim that `Storage.Create` is an unexpected call/panic and that the unified-store failure path is not exercised is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go — Async legacy calls make test results timing-dependent: tests return before the goroutine runs, so any future assertion on legacy mock counts would be flaky; tests should synchronize with the goroutine or inject the timeout/clock

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Mode3 now performs legacy writes/deletes/updates asynchronously via `go func(){ ... d.Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection ... }()` with a 10s timeout. In the new pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go tests, calls like `dw.Create(...)`/`dw.Delete(...)` return immediately without any synchronization to ensure the legacy goroutine has run. So any attempt to assert legacy mock calls (e.g., counts/expectations) would be timing-dependent/flaky unless the test waits (e.g., via channel/WaitGroup) or the implementation allows injection of timing/async behavior.
